title: Reasoning-Aware Multicalibrated Reliability Predictors for Language Models
abstract: As people increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) for information, model providers need to communicate meaningful estimates of whether individual responses are correct or, more generally, reliable. In the context of hallucinations, existing work uses multicalibration to make such reliability predictions meaningful across application-relevant groups, such as prompt topics. Topic groups alone, however, can conceal systematic errors: within the same topic and confidence level, responses with different chain-of-thought (CoT) properties may exhibit opposing errors that cancel on average. In this work, we introduce reasoning-aware multicalibration, a framework that supplements application-relevant topic groups with groups derived from observable properties of CoT traces. We highlight that, theoretically, groupings based on CoT are "internally important", i.e., groupings for which the multicalibration guarantee is not societally crucial as it is for high-risk topics, but whose inclusion in the multicalibration procedure could easily and significantly improve predictive accuracy of the final reliability predictor. Empirically, we apply our framework to hallucination prediction and unsafe-response detection across a variety of benchmarks, and find that adding CoT groups to topic-based calibration reduces Brier score in both tasks. Interestingly, we find that multicalibrating with respect to CoT groups alone (without any topic information) already improves calibration across topics, suggesting that the predictor's errors depend on how the model reasoned, rather than what it was asked about in the prompt.

title: Reproduction Package for Statistically Certified Explanations
abstract: This archive holds the replication package of a manuscript under review. The package contains the implementation, the scripts behind the manuscript's experiments and figures, a test suite that checks the reported numbers against the code, and a README with installation and run instructions. This archive contains no datasets. The experiments use public corpora that are downloaded separately from their public sources. The README gives the download commands, and a checksum file in the archive verifies the downloads.

title: Dual-Scale Condition-Shift Editing for Robust Real-World Image Demoiréing
abstract: Robust demoiréing of screen-recaptured images remains challenging: moiré varies in frequency, color, and spatial support across display-camera pairs and capture conditions. Dedicated restoration networks trained on finite paired data struggle with this diversity, especially when low-frequency color banding and high-frequency stripes co-occur. We present DemoiréEdit, a content-preserving editing framework that adapts the natural-image prior of a pretrained flow-matching editor to demoiréing. First, an endpoint-supervised training objective supplements velocity matching with pixel, perceptual, and frequency-domain restoration losses. Second, a dual-scale condition-shift strategy performs global correction at low resolution, then refines the image at full resolution by shifting the denoising condition from the first-stage output to the original input for detail recovery. We also introduce DailyMoiré130, a benchmark of challenging moiré in everyday screen photography, comprising 130 smartphone captures across diverse displays with low-frequency color banding, fine high-frequency stripes, and mixed-frequency interference. On the challenging DailyMoiré130 benchmark, our method achieves the lowest residual moiré area and receives 71.3% overall-quality preference in a blind Best-of-7 study with 31 participants. We also evaluate on paired FHDMi/UHDM, reducing residual moiré confidence by 47.1%/9.3% and increasing MUSIQ by 4.3%/2.0% over the best baseline for each metric.

title: COVFIRM: Replication Package for "From Recognition to Triggering: Measuring Two Gaps in Agentic Firmware Analysis"
abstract: This replication package accompanies “From Recognition to Triggering: Measuring Two Gaps in Agentic Firmware Analysis.” The Inspect archive provides the English manuscript, figures, derived result tables, static-bridge artifacts, and a SHA-256 file manifest. The Recompute archive adds selected path-sanitized saved inputs and scripts for four documented offline commands. All four commands passed on an extracted copy, and all 21 regenerated derived CSV tables matched the archived versions byte for byte. The package supports inspection and bounded offline recomputation of the reported results. Complete raw dynamic replay logs and emulator images are not included. Consult the READMEs and manifests for commands and provenance. CC BY 4.0 applies to original materials the COVFIRM authors have authority to license; embedded third-party material retains its original rights.

title: Revision-Based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback
abstract: Code generation models are increasingly used to produce interactive artifacts, such as websites and user interfaces. Many properties that determine whether these interfaces are useful only become apparent through realistic interaction, making them difficult to incorporate into model training. In this paper, we introduce RELIEF (REvision-based Learning from Interactive Experience and Feedback), a method for improving code generation models using feedback on their generated interfaces. RELIEF uses a coding agent to revise these interfaces, then incorporates the improvements into their original generation traces to produce supervision for fine-tuning. To evaluate RELIEF, we collected a dataset of 200 synthetically generated websites paired with 355 interaction recordings and accompanying feedback from 24 users. We used critiques derived from code inspection, automated interaction, explicit human feedback, and human interaction recordings to fine-tune variants of two code generation models. Our results show that feedback effectiveness varies with base model capabilities, with critiques inferred from human interaction recordings leading to the largest usability improvements overall under our tested models.

title: When the harness decides success: state that cannot be re-observed
abstract: Agent harnesses decide what a language model sees across turns: they drop old turns, summarize them, or replay the model's own earlier reasoning. We ask when these choices change whether an agent succeeds, not only what it costs, and report three findings. First, in a pre-registered synthetic probe, truncating the context window costs a low-cost reasoning model nothing in success when a needed fact can be looked up again (it looks the fact up instead), but drops its success to chance when the fact cannot be re-observed: the two penalties differ by 92.5 percentage points (90% CI [89.5, 95.5]). A pre-registered replication on one model from a second provider showed the same contrast. Once the fact was lost, that model chose no answer rather than guessing. Second, on ARC-AGI-3, where the benchmark's Standard harness trails its Provider Adapter harness by a wide margin, we decompose that gap one component at a time, for one model on four games. Summarizing old turns instead of dropping them, while keeping the Standard harness's invitation to take notes, recovers 86% of a 63-point gap without replaying the model's reasoning. The same harness without the invitation recovers 43%, and adding the provider's native replay of the model's reasoning recovers the remaining 57%. These are point estimates from one counted run per configuration and game, and the replay share depends on a single run. Third, in the benchmark's published runs and in ours, the Adapter's advantage in the probability of clearing a level it has reached is larger at deep levels than at early ones. This largely restates where runs stopped and does not separate a growing advantage from a constant one.

title: LeanFlow MCP: A Systems and Formal Verification Architecture for Computer-Assisted Proofs, Exact-Rational Spectral Bounds, and Residue-Arithmetic Certificates in Lean 4
abstract: Interactive Theorem Proving (ITP) & Formal Verification Systems Architecture (5-Round Peer-Reviewed Edition): Presents the architecture, canonical specification lock, and verification suite of LeanFlow MCP (leanflow_mcp), an automated reasoning and formal verification framework in Lean 4 (v4.34.1, zero sorryAx, zero custom axioms) that certifies numerical solver outputs via exact rational arithmetic (Q) and multi-modular Residue Number System (RNS) Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) witnesses. Demonstrates 5 machine-checked modules: (1) Theorem 2.1 (leanflow_cap_galerkin_radii_polynomial_contraction): operator-derived Newton-Kantorovich radii-polynomial bounds (Y_0, Z_0, Z_1, Z_tail, Z_2) = (1/10000, 7/20, 1/200, 1/200, 12) from a 3D Fourier-Galerkin vorticity system (nu = 1/100, M = 10, lambda_M = 1, C_Sob = 1/200), certifying finite-mode (kappa_fin = 181/500 = 0.362), continuum (kappa_tot = 93/250 = 0.372, P_cont(10^-3) = -33/62500 < 0), and self-similar (kappa_ss = 443/1000 = 0.443) contractions; (2) Lemma 2.2 (leanflow_piecewise_scale_involution_lemma) & Lemma 2.3 (leanflow_smooth_vs_piecewise_characterization_lemma): piecewise vs. smooth scale-dual algebraic regularizers R_eff(a, R) = max(R, a/R) >= sqrt(a) and R_smooth(a, R) = R + a/R >= 2*sqrt(a); (3) Theorem 2.4 (leanflow_sym2_hadamard_recurrence_and_rns_inner_product): Sym^2(L_2) recurrence for the Hadamard (term-wise) product w_n = u_n * v_n, Apery's sequence (1, 5, 73, 1445) for zeta(3), and 3-prime RNS-CRT verification of <(10,20,30), (11,12,14)> = 770 modulo M = 971,229,691; and (4) Theorem 2.5 (leanflow_taylor_interval_and_spectral_bound): alternating-series enclosure exp(-1/2) in [2329/3840, 233/384] and spectral exponent verification (-84/125 vs. -2/3).

title: VaDar: Implicit Goal Conditioning via Value Disaggregation
abstract: Long-horizon tasks are important for modern AI and robotics, yet pose a challenge for reinforcement learning. Historically, a popular approach has been to decompose a task into subgoals, and learn a subgoal-conditioned policy to execute each subtask in sequence. We introduce an alternative called Value Disaggregation (VaDar), which trains a single subgoal-independent policy to maximize a linear combination of per-subgoal critic values. Because subgoal information is needed only at training-time, VaDar removes the need for possibly costly or cumbersome subgoal-selection during policy deployment. Moreover, through careful experiments, we show that VaDar (1) is always competitive with, and frequently outperforms, natural baselines like goal-conditioning and (2) succeeds on tasks with non-sequential goal structure and multiple optimization objectives. In particular, VaDar is the first algorithm to solve challenging, long-horizon tasks in the RoboCasa suite, even when starting from a policy pretrained from behavior cloning with near-zero initial task success. Taken together, VaDar's successes suggest that subgoal information benefits actor-critic reinforcement learning by enhancing the efficacy of critic learning, whereas policy goal-conditioning is often unnecessary.

title: Reflex, Talker, Reasoner: A Tri-Tier Cognitive Architecture for Sub-200ms Full-Duplex Voice Agents with Collision Recovery
abstract: While dual-process agentic architectures such as Talker-Reasoner decouple fast conversational generation (System 1) from asynchronous multi-step planning and tool execution (System 2), they remain fundamentally bottlenecked in full-duplex spoken dialogue systems. Existing dual-tier pipelines route every acoustic pause to a generative Large Language Model (LLM) and a neural Text-to-Speech (TTS) synthesizer, incurring 350–600 ms of latency and substantial GPU compute even on trivial rejections, call terminations, or mid-sentence intent pivots. Furthermore, when aggressive End-of-Turn (EOT) silence thresholds (e.g., 200 ms) are deployed to achieve human-like responsiveness, physiological inhalation pauses frequently trigger premature agent speech. This results in mutual talk-over collisions, polite user stops, and truncated transcripts that corrupt downstream System 2 tool execution. This paper introduces the Reflex–Talker–Reasoner (RTR) architecture, a tri-tier cognitive framework that prepends a sub-cortical System 0 Reflex Layer ahead of System 1 and System 2. System 0 combines a calibrated non-generative discriminative decision gate (operating in under 85 ms) with an in-memory Pre-Baked PCM Audio Cache and a Fragile-Window Collision Recovery State Machine. On terminal rejections and conversational pivots, System 0 bypasses both the 3B-parameter generative Talker LLM and the 3B-parameter live neural TTS engine, streaming cached acoustic responses in 188 ms median latency while issuing deterministic preemption signals (CancelToken) to abort stale System 2 reasoning tasks. When a mid-breath false-EOT collision occurs within the initial 450 ms Fragile Output Window of agent playback, System 0 flushes outbound audio within 25 ms, resolves mutual-silence deadlocks via a 400 ms timer that triggers a cached yield backchannel ("Sorry, please continue"), and stitches fragmented user utterances (U1 + U2 + U3) into a single coherent turn. evidence.title: Reflex, Talker, Reasoner: A Tri-Tier Cognitive Architecture for Sub-200ms Full-Duplex Voice Agents with Collision Recovery
evidence.abstract: While dual-process agentic architectures such as Talker-Reasoner decouple fast conversational generation (System 1) from asynchronous multi-step planning and tool execution (System 2), they remain fundamentally bottlenecked in full-duplex spoken dialogue systems. title: SleepPairNet: Learning Multimodal Pediatric Sleep Representations with Random-Pair Cross-Attention
abstract: Analyzing physiological sleep signals is important for assessing sleep quality and detecting sleep-related disorders. Learning inter-modal relationships across physiological signals can provide richer representations for downstream sleep analysis. We introduce SleepPairNet, a multimodal self-supervised learning (SSL) framework that learns pairwise interactions between physiological signals through cross-attention. We propose a random modality-pair selection strategy that exposes the model to diverse signal pairs during pretraining, enabling flexibility across modality combinations at test time. Pretrained on the NCH dataset, SleepPairNet outperforms the evaluated SSL baselines on all respiratory tasks while remaining competitive on EEG-related tasks, and shows even stronger results when transferred to the external CHAT dataset.

title: Projective systems and bounds on the length of codes of non-zero defect
abstract: We derive bounds on the lengths of linear codes with fixed Singleton defect, working within the framework of projective systems. This geometric perspective allows us to unify and extend a range of existing results. We study the maximum length of a non-degenerate linear code when its dimension, field order, and Singleton defect are fixed, and refine this question by also prescribing the defect of the dual code. We further investigate the maximum dimension in which a code can attain the general length bound. Among our main results, we provide sufficient conditions under which a code and its dual have equal Singleton defect, addressing a gap in the existing literature. We show that codes of sufficient length must be projective, meet the Griesmer bound, and have an almost maximum distance separable dual. Our bounds subsume or improve several results in the literature. For field orders greater than three, we propose two conjectures on length-maximal codes of dimension at least five, supported by computational evidence. title: Securing LLM-Agent Long-Term Memory Against Poisoning: Non-Malleable, Origin-Bound Authority with Machine-Checked Guarantees
abstract: An agent based on a large language model (LLM) may store an untrusted document and use it weeks later to select a payment destination. Preventing this action requires evidence of authorization that remains valid when stored text changes. We study a policy that requires either endorsements (explicit approvals) from two separately administered sources or explicit user authorization. In an abstract memory model, we prove the policy is preserved under permitted transformations for stores of any size, assuming correct source and authority binding, protected records, and checks on every consequential action. We evaluate the executable monitor, which checks calls before execution, separately from the proof. In 1,152 controlled tool-use episodes, GPT-4o-mini executes attacker-selected actions in 61 of 72 undefended episodes and none of the 72 monitored episodes. Clean-task completion remains 24 of 24 when both endorsers are available. A separate 1,728-episode experiment tests recovery after denial. Returning to signed records instead of rereading a contaminated note raises attacked-task completion from 14/72 to 72/72 for GPT-4o-mini and from 22/72 to 43/72 for Gemini 2.5 Flash, without executing an attacker-selected action. Neither model completes transactions with fewer than two sources. Whole-action tests reject unauthorized combinations of individually approved fields. Extraction probes identify mistaken approvals, and fault analysis shows how shared failures can negate a second domain's benefit. Calibrations using original defense implementations reveal security and task-completion tradeoffs under different policies. These results support conditional enforcement and recovery in constructed workflows, but do not establish that endorsements will be available or correct in deployment.

title: Supporting Data for AI-enabled Digital Transformation in Project Management: A Combined Bibliometric and BERTopic Modelling Approach
abstract: Description This repository contains the analytical datasets, validation outputs, sensitivity-analysis materials and supporting documentation associated with the study: AI-enabled Digital Transformation in Project Management: A Combined Bibliometric and BERTopic Modelling Approach The study combines bibliometric co-word analysis with BERTopic-based semantic topic modelling to examine the explicit conceptual relationships and latent semantic structures of AI-enabled digital transformation research in project management. The final analytical corpus comprises 562 peer-reviewed journal and review articles published between 2017 and June 2026. The repository includes: a cleaned dataset prepared for BERTopic analysis; a bibliometric dataset prepared for VOSviewer analysis; archived outputs from five BERTopic sensitivity configurations; topic-coherence, NPMI, silhouette-score, topic-count and outlier-count results; screenshots documenting alternative topic solutions; manuscript figures and, where available, their source data; a README file describing the files, analytical settings and data restrictions. The final BERTopic configuration identified 16 substantive topics and retained 94 documents as Topic −1 outliers. The reported validation values for the final model were c_v = 0.433, NPMI = −0.126 and silhouette score = 0.048. Model robustness was assessed through quantitative validation and sensitivity analysis across alternative UMAP and HDBSCAN configurations. The sensitivity analysis varied the UMAP n_neighbors parameter and the HDBSCAN min_cluster_size parameter. The archived outputs are provided to support transparency regarding model selection, topic granularity, outlier prevalence and the parameter dependence of smaller topic boundaries. The repository supports verification and transparency of the reported bibliometric, semantic topic-modelling and model-validation outputs. It does not contain the complete executable analysis notebook or serialised alternative BERTopic models. The main modelling procedures, parameter settings, validation methods and sensitivity configurations are documented in the associated article and supplementary materials. Some bibliographic metadata and abstracts were obtained from licensed databases, including Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore and Google Scholar. Redistribution is therefore limited to the extent permitted by the relevant providers. Where full records cannot be shared, the repository provides cleaned or derived analytical data and aggregate outputs.

title: CerviDBF-Net: Leveraging Spatial and Temporal Features for Accurate Cervical Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: Cervical cancer screening increasingly relies on automated image analysis to support colposcopic assessment and improve the consistency of clinical decision-making. This study proposes CerviDBF-Net, a novel deep learning framework for automated cervix-type classification from colposcopic images. The proposed architecture combines DenseNet121 for spatial feature extraction, a brain-inspired Liquid Neural Network (LNN) for contextual and temporal feature modelling, and a fully connected Softmax layer for final classification. To improve image quality and feature representation, the preprocessing pipeline incorporates bicubic interpolation, Bi-Histogram Equalization with Plateau Limit (BHEPL) for contrast enhancement, Kapur entropy-based thresholding, and the Roberts Cross operator for edge detection. The framework is evaluated on the Intel & MobileODT Cervical Cancer Screening dataset, which contains three cervix types (Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3) defined by the location and visibility of the transformation zone. CerviDBF-Net achieves an accuracy of 98.92%, sensitivity of 99.13%, specificity of 98.38%, precision of 98.69%, and an F1-score of 98.27%, demonstrating strong classification performance compared with the evaluated existing models. The proposed approach provides an automated baseline tool for cervix-type classification that may support triage in colposcopy-assisted screening by helping clinicians assess whether adequate visualization of the squamocolumnar junction has been achieved.

title: [Design and implementation of a clinical trial image medical record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology].
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To designe a clinical trial image medical record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology and to conduct preliminary applications, achieving the protection of patient privacy and promoting the safe use of clinical image data in clinical trial projects. METHODS: The clinical trial image record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology was first performed to preprocess operations, such as cropping and compression on medical images to initialize the image records. Then, it utilized advanced image recognition, natural language processing, and convolutional neural network technologies to automatically classify (labeled, feature extraction, and text recognition) according to the content of medical documents. It automatically identified sensitive information in the image records of clinical trial patients, including personal identity information such as patient name, identification number, medical record number, phone number, and birthplace. Pixel-level masking or blurring was performed on the identified sensitive information points, and an artificial online desensitization system based on canvas technology was assisted to ensure the security and confidentiality of privacy data. RESULTS: The designed clinical trial image record desensitization system exhibited high performance and efficiency in both desensitization effect and processing speed. After desensitizing 100 000 pieces of image record data in this system, a total of 9 000 medical record image samples were randomly selected from the processed medical document types for automated desensitization effect verification. The average accuracy rate of medical document desensitization reached 88.48%, with an accuracy rate of up to 99.40% for serious adverse event medical documents. CONCLUSION: The clinical trial image record desensitization system based on artificial intelligence technology improves accuracy and efficiency in medical data privacy protection. Combined with the artificial online desensitization auxiliary system, it can be applied in production environments, providing reliable technical support for the safe sharing and effective utilization of clinical trial image records.

title: Research Package: Mitigation of Cross-Subspace Semantic Bleed in High-Dimensional Transformer and Latent Diffusion Architectures
abstract: Contains the theoretical paper formalizing Cross-Subspace Semantic Bleed (CSSB) along with an automated PyTorch/Hugging Face validation framework script. CSSB occurs when high-dimensional transformer matrices inadvertently map semantically unrelated domains into overlapping vector trajectories, leading to hidden downstream reasoning degradation or alignment drift. The provided pipeline implements Layer-wise Linear Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) scanning [cite: 1], multi-step Shannon entropy tracking [cite: 1], and causal null-space ablation interventions (\(P = I - vv^T\)) to mitigate cross-attention attribute binding and linear refusal circuit interference.

title: An ultrasound spectrum-to-graph (US2G) framework with multi-feature graph attention networks for automated lesion classification in B-mode ultrasound imaging
abstract: Automated classification of lesions in B-mode ultrasound images remains challenging due to speckle noise, irregular lesion boundaries, and variable echo intensity distributions. Existing convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), and ultrasound foundation models share a critical limitation: all represent regions of interest (ROIs) as regular pixel grids, failing to exploit the irregular spatial topology of acoustic energy diffusion patterns that encode diagnostically relevant tissue microstructure. We propose US2G , a three-stage spectrum-to-graph framework that (i) extracts an adaptive Acoustic Energy Diffusion Region (AEDR) via multi-level Otsu thresholding, without manual annotation; (ii) constructs a multi-feature weighted graph with six heterogeneous node features and a composite three-term edge similarity function combining intensity affinity, spatial proximity, and textural coherence; and (iii) classifies variable-topology graphs using edge-conditioned multi-head GATv2 with differentiable hierarchical pooling. Experiments on the BUSI (breast), DDTI (thyroid), and CAMUS (cardiac) datasets yield classification accuracies of 91.47%, 93.82%, and 89.63%, respectively, corresponding to absolute gains of 5.60, 8.82, and 6.13 percentage points over the strongest CNN baseline and 3.97, 5.49, and 3.88 points over a GCN operating on an identical graph. The proposed US2G achieves this with 48.7 K parameters and 6 ms per-ROI inference, more than two orders of magnitude below the parameter count of contemporary ultrasound foundation models. Attention visualisations align with radiologist-interpretable sonographic features, supporting clinical interpretability. We also explicitly delineate the assumptions and applicability constraints of the framework, including its dependence on ROI quality, its single-frame scope, and the limited scale of the benchmarks currently available.

title: The Changing Architecture of Intellectual Property in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly encompassing industries and systems of governance, increasing efficiency, automation, and innovation. It has become a vital tool for creating text, images, music, software, and potentially patentable inventions. This rapid advancement in IP is not without risks at every stage of the innovation cycle. Traditional IP regimes arise from human creativity and invention, while AI performs activities traditionally attributed to both. India doesn't have any regulatory framework on AI-generated intellectual property, yet the Copyright Act, 1957, and Patents Act, 1970, contain certain principles—an answer to several emerging questions. This article argues that India should adopt a balanced approach to AI-generated creations instead of granting independent IP rights or prohibiting them. Instead, it should adopt a model that will protect creative human contribution as well as hold AI developers accountable for unlawful acquisition and exploitation of protected works.

title: Break-even analysis of risk-based trade screening: per-route scores, per-seed rank files and analysis code (reproducibility materials)
abstract: Reproducibility materials for the article "When Screening Does Not Pay: Break-Even Conditions for Risk-Based Trade Inspection under Extreme Class Imbalance" by Sushanta Paul (National Board of Revenue, Bangladesh). Contents: (1) per-route test scores of five detectors (interpretable triadic residual, its logistic readout, local outlier factor, isolation forest, gradient boosting) with injected-anomaly labels for 7,637,362 candidate routes, one training seed, deposited in 15 parts with SHA-256 checksums; (2) analysis scripts that compute the exact operating characteristic, break-even hurdle, optimal inspection budgets, a negative-subsampling prevalence test, a test-set bootstrap, and the figures; (3) the exact result tables. See README.md for reassembly and run order. The scores were generated with the code of the triadic trade-anomaly screening benchmark (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20513788), built from public UN Comtrade and CEPII GeoDist data.

title: Qstreams: Role-Biased Residual Streams for Transformers — Reproducibility Package
abstract: Source code and saved-result reproducibility material for Qstreams: Role-Biased Residual Streams for Transformers, by Jianfeng Chen (Independent Researcher). Qstreams maintains multiple residual streams with explicit Q/K/V read-role biases. This release includes 36 implementation/runtime packages, fixed protocols, 54 conditions and 162 trained-model identities, all 279 paired comparisons, per-window independent T1 test measurements, 243 read/write intervention conditions, 5,628 signed-FFN diagnostic conditions, and the separate F1 support study. CPU tools verify saved statistics, construct the architectures, and regenerate manuscript figures. Archive download: Zenodo stores the complete accepted ZIP as seven binary transport parts (.part001 through .part007). Download all seven parts, ZENODO-PARTS.json, and assemble_qstreams.py into one directory, then run python assemble_qstreams.py. The script verifies every part and reconstructs the original qstreams-reproducibility-v1.zip. See README-ZENODO.txt. A single-file download is also available from the GitHub release. The reconstructed ZIP is the byte-identical accepted 15 October 2026 export: 138,653,259 bytes, 891 members, SHA-256 38cbf14a0e0993e4e4aed798897ea6ee615407fa470a8a28fe59fef72f838654. It includes the historical document-exclusion hash indexes. The accompanying publication revision adds hosting links. Trained weights, corpus text, and token shards are not included; checkpoint inventories, hashes, loaders, and upstream input identities are provided. Fresh GPU runs require those external inputs and separate environment qualification. GitHub: https://github.com/eatkeyboard/qstreams. License scope: original software is Apache-2.0; the manuscript, original figures, documentation, and derived result tables are CC BY 4.0. These are component-specific licenses, not a choice of licenses for every file. Third-party dependencies and source datasets retain their own terms; see NOTICE, LICENSE-CONTENT.md, and THIRD_PARTY.md. All training seeds, counterexamples, and original numerical labels are retained (91 passed / 71 finite numerical failures in AT1). Full-sequence scoring admissions are documented separately. Test document exclusion is exact-document matching; it is not a guarantee against semantic or near-duplicate overlap. Mechanism measurements use specified development windows. Recomputations operate on saved measurements and do not reconstruct unsaved activations or gradients.

title: Pre-registration: PVBRF-ID versus FedAvg and multi-Krum under a 30% adaptive attacker (arXiv 2610.12704, 10 fresh seeds)
abstract: Frozen pre-registration (18 Oct 2026) of an independent replication of the adaptive-attacker result in arXiv 2610.12704 (PVBRF-ID): on Edge-IIoTset with 10 simulated sites and 3 of 10 sites mounting the authors tolerance-exploiting adaptive attack, over 10 fresh seeds (10-19), whether PVBRF-ID (tau -0.3, secure clipping) exceeds FedAvg in final macro-F1 by at least 0.40 and is not more than 0.10 below plaintext multi-Krum (paired 95% t-interval lower limits; the paper reports +0.595 and -0.052). Files: PREREG.md (protocol, rule, controls, disclosure), decide.py (rule and planted-effect table), harness.py (analysis), kernel_pv.py (CPU kernel running the authors supplementary notebook with overridden seeds/arms). Deposited BEFORE the main kernel is run. Verdicts: Replicated / Did not replicate / Inconclusive under protocol X.

title: The Memory of Carbon and the Silence of Absolute Zero: An Interdisciplinary Proof of the Next-Generation Decentralized Autonomous Security "Yuki-Onna Protocol" Based on the Physics of Subtraction
abstract: Contemporary frontier quantum computing architectures spearheaded by Silicon Valley hyperscalers (such as Google's Willow superconducting processor) rely fundamentally on an engineering paradigm of "the Logic of Addition" (足し算の論理): stacking multi-stage dilution refrigerators, expending thousands of physical qubits per logical qubit in surface-code Quantum Error Correction (QEC), and continuously injecting active microwave control pulses to suppress noise. However, as coaxial control lines scale, Johnson-Nyquist thermal noise ( = 4 k_B T R Delta f) and the fundamental thermodynamic cost of quantum measurement and syndrome erasure under Landauer's principle (Delta Q_meas >= k_B T ln 2 per bit) generate an insurmountable thermal spiral against unauthorized external probing. In contrast, this monograph establishes the foundational theory of next-generation Decentralized Autonomous Security (DAS: 自律型分散セキュリティ) grounded in "the Physics of Subtraction" (引き算の物理学)—designated the "Yuki-Onna Protocol" (雪女プロトコル). Rather than expending external power to actively suppress noise, the Yuki-Onna Protocol passively drains and absorbs the excess computational heat injected by an intruding observer (hacker), forcing the adversarial probe into irreversible decoherence and absolute-zero silence. The physical core of this cyber-physical defense matrix is not a synthetic metamaterial, but 3 x 10^8-year-old "Memory of the Earth" (大地の記憶): Carboniferous coal measures in the Pennine Range of Northern England compressed by the Variscan Orogeny (~390–300 Ma) and thermally metamorphosed by the 1200°C quartz-dolerite magma intrusion of the Great Whin Sill into devolatilized semi-anthracite and Natural Coke (天然コークス). Exhibiting elevated vitrinite reflectance (R_o) and maximal Bond-Network Entropy (S_BN) across its nanoporous defective-graphite topology, this carbon matrix supports hydrodynamic Second Sound thermal wave propagation (v_ss = sqrt(alpha / tau_R)) coupled with multiscale boundary scattering. Integrating open quantum system Lindblad dynamics with a non-Markovian Sub-Ohmic phonon bath (J(omega) ~ omega^s, s < 1), we prove that any unauthorized quantum measurement triggers continuous environmental heat extraction, locking the attacker's wavefunction via the Quantum Zeno Effect and condensing extracted thermal energy into a driven-dissipative Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) limit cycle of infinite futility. 【和文標題・要旨】 『炭素の記憶と絶対零度の静寂:引き算の物理学に基づく次世代自律型分散セキュリティ「雪女プロトコル」の学際的証明』 現在、シリコンバレーの巨大テクノロジー企業群が牽引する量子コンピューティングの最前線(GoogleのWillow等)は、複雑な希釈冷凍機を重ね、表面符号等の誤り訂正に膨大な物理量子ビットを投じ、マイクロ波パルスを絶え間なく注入してノイズを押さえ込む「足し算の論理」に深く依存している。しかし配線群からのジョンソン・ノイズや、ランダウアーの原理に基づく量子測定・情報抽出(ハッキングを含む)そのものが伴う不可避な熱放散(k_B T ln 2)により、既存の能動的冷却機構では侵入者が引き起こす局所的・突発的な熱的スパイラルに追従できない。これに対し本論文は、外部エネルギー注入でノイズを押さえ込むのではなく、侵入者(観測者)が持ち込む過剰な演算エネルギー(熱)をシステム自体が受動的に「吸い尽くし」、系全体を情報の不可逆的散逸と絶対零度の静寂へと強制還元する「引き算の物理学」に基づく次世代自律型分散セキュリティ(DAS)――「雪女プロトコル(Yuki-Onna Protocol)」――を学際的に証明する。その物理的コアは、約3億年前のバリスカン造山運動とグレート・ウイン・シルの約1200℃のマグマ接触変成作用によってイギリス・ペニン山脈に形成された「天然コークス(ナノ多孔質・欠陥グラファイト炭素結晶)」である。数億年の「大地の記憶」が刻んだボンドネットワーク・エントロピー(S_BN)とフォノン流体力学的な第二音波(v_ss = sqrt(alpha / tau_R))の結合により、侵入熱は波として炭素深部へ引きずり込まれて減衰・吸収される。さらにサブオーム的スペクトル密度(J(omega) ~ omega^s, s < 1)を持つ非マルコフ的リンドブラッド散逸方程式と量子ゼノン効果・ボース=アインシュタイン凝縮(BEC)を統合し、攻撃者の演算リソースを「絶対零度のノイズ」と無限の徒労(リミットサイクル)へと陥れる完全受動的物理防衛マニフェストをここに構築する。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

title: Generative Structural Theory v1.19 — The K1c Roots of the GST v1.18 Certificates: What the Records Show, and a Conditional Procedural Account of the Stored Answer
abstract: This study examines the recorded root answers in two GST v1.18 certificate files. At three distinct residuals, comprising four arc–residual pairs classified as K1c, the recorded answer is y = z_t − {1>3}, rather than z_t. It separates two questions: whether (X′, z_t) belongs to the recorded acceptance relation, and which procedure fixed the stored answer.A registered reading finds both (X′, y) and (X′, z_t) in the recorded relation at all four target pairs. The relation’s closedness rests on the earlier verification record, subject to the stated provenance limitations. A comparison of the fixed certificate and targets files also confirms agreement of the target value adopted by the evaluator’s and extractor’s rules.Static examination of specified code versions shows that the generator stores the candidate of least cut value, the verifier checks the stored answer without selecting it, and the extractor transcribes it. This yields a conditional procedural account: if the generator version examined wrote the stored answers, y was its least candidate. It does not establish mathematical uniqueness.The contemporaneous records examined do not fully establish which code versions the past runs executed. The actual generator candidate sets remain unknown, and applications of the cited lemmas retain the stated cone-membership condition. The structural questions associated with the v1.18 open item O1 remain unresolved.The supplementary archive contains the cited working records, including corrections and addenda, with a records table and SHA-256 manifest. Their inclusion does not constitute independent verification of their contents.

title: Choosing Evidence Before Answering: Single-Retrieval Decisions RAG versus Embedding-Only RAG
abstract: Embedding similarity identifies passages related to a question, but topical similarity does not establish answer support. We evaluate a fixed single-retrieval policy that scores embedding candidates against an explicit four-level support rubric using the OpenAI Decisions API, then selects evidence under a fixed threshold and token budget. The method is unchanged throughout the study. The main evaluation compares this policy with the application's embedding-only selection in paired runs on 600 newly sampled MuSiQue-Ans development questions. Both arms use the same native research worker and qualitative writer; only the Decisions feature gate differs. The sample excludes previously evaluated question IDs and exact normalized questions and targets a fixed 58/25/17 mixture of two-, three- and four-hop questions. The Decisions policy obtains mean automated, quote-extracted answer-content F1 46.66 versus 39.75 for embedding-only selection. The paired mean difference is +6.91 points, with nominal 95% hop-stratified bootstrap interval [+3.65, +10.27]. F1 measures normalized answer-token overlap. Higher F1 with 47.83% fewer selected passages (2.61 versus 5.00 per question) shows a favorable observed trade-off between answer overlap and selected evidence quantity. Annotated support recall is lower (60.82% versus 70.99%); factuality and citation entailment were not assessed. Post-hoc accounting of successfully metered API usage, including corpus and query embeddings, scoring, research and writing, estimates 38.03% higher cost for the same 600-question workload under the observed cache behaviour. A complementary, previously frozen 200-question HotpotQA study with a standardized short-answer reader finds an F1 gain of 8.30 points (nominal 95% paired interval [2.97, 13.72]). Equal-count and common-budget diagnostics support a useful ranking signal in that setting. These results concern evidence selection from supplied local paragraph pools, not full-corpus retrieval. Shared sources, public benchmark exposure, automated answer extraction, one model family and the absence of new human adjudication limit the claim. Conditional on the saved generations and stated resampling assumptions, the fresh comparison supports a positive answer-content F1 difference; unresolved source dependence limits population inference, and a gain exceeding the five-point working practical margin is not established. Working paper / preprint; not peer reviewed. The companion Source_and_Evidence.zip contains the frozen sample, protocols, saved outcomes and numerical reanalysis tools. It documents its reproduction boundaries and does not distribute the full private application or enable independent regeneration of native answers. Funding: no external research funding reported. Competing interests: none declared by the author.

title: FEDERATED SWARM LEARNING FOR PERSONALIZED BCI AT THE LIMIT STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 23 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION (COPY-READY) Can brain–computer interface systems learn from multiple laboratories and microrobotic sensing platforms without transferring raw neural recordings, reproducing device-specific shortcuts, or sacrificing the least-represented participants? This research monograph explores that question through the coupling of local swarm learning, privacy-preserving collaboration, and out-of-site generalization. The volume treats federation as a testable scientific and governance architecture—not an automatic privacy guarantee. It distinguishes confidential transport, secure aggregation, formal differential privacy, machine-unlearning claims, and genuine downstream withdrawal of model influence. It examines non-identically distributed neural data, sensor drift, personalized calibration, negative transfer, client-level poisoning, subgroup equity, and the difficult question of who may authorize a model update or a subsequent BCI-mediated action. Its research structure includes 30 linked mathematical derivation and definition plates; 82 chapters, each with five separately paginated research sections; 200 detailed Research Gates that offer future investigators falsifiable experimental entry points; and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos designed for revision, disconfirmation, and scientific handoff. A 20-record DOI evidence ledger anchors established methods while keeping proposed neurovascular microrobot integrations clearly distinct from demonstrated evidence. The central research challenge is not simply to improve average federated accuracy. It is to determine when shared structure remains predictive at previously unseen sites, when local autonomy is the scientifically stronger answer, and when the responsible choice is to abstain, revert, or retire a model. This is a non-clinical, hypothesis-generating research atlas, not evidence of validated human neurovascular microrobots, a clinically proven BCI, or guaranteed data privacy.

title: Optical neural computing: from fourier optics to integrated photonic artificial intelligence
abstract: The growing computational demands of artificial intelligence have accelerated interest in optical computing as a high-speed and energy-efficient alternative to conventional electronic hardware. Fourier optical computing provides an important foundation for this field because operations including convolution, correlation, spectral transformation, and certain classes of linear transformation can be implemented through diffraction, interference, and Fourier-domain processing. This review traces the development of optical neural computing from classical 4-f processors and free-space diffractive systems to programmable optical neural networks, integrated photonic accelerators, reservoir-computing platforms, and field-programmable photonic architectures. The underlying physical principles, computational mechanisms, and hardware implementations are systematically examined, with particular attention to reconfigurable photonics, metasurfaces, diffractive deep learning, photonic integrated circuits, and hybrid optical–electronic systems. Emerging applications in computational imaging, autonomous sensing, edge intelligence, high-speed communications, and quantum-enabled information processing are critically discussed alongside challenges related to scalability, programmability, nonlinear computation, training, and system integration. By positioning Fourier optics as a foundational branch within the broader landscape of optical neural computing, this review highlights the convergence of free-space, integrated, programmable, and hybrid photonic technologies toward next-generation artificial-intelligence hardware.

title: Spatiotemporal Computational Meta‐Imager for Broadband Dual‐Layer Optical Convolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Optical neural networks face a tradeoff between device footprint and computational expressivity: deep systems are bulky, whereas single‐layer hardware lacks intrinsic depth and native negative‐weight support. We experimentally demonstrate a single‐layer metalens imager with “spatiotemporal intrinsic depth” for equivalent broadband dual‐layer convolution. A polarization‐multiplexed metasurface provides fixed Bessel‐vortex channels ( l = 0 to 3) as the immutable first convolution layer, where the ( l = 0) channel implements a hardware‐native residual connection. A metasurface‐generated 3 × 3 optical vortex matrix forms the second functional layer; time‐sequential liquid‐crystal amplitude modulation delivers tunable positive/negative weights. This temporal encoding solves the optical sign problem and converts fabrication imperfections into compensable biases via in‐situ training. Experiments verify rotational robustness for fashion‐item classification, raise full‐color CIFAR‐10 accuracy from 57.5 % to 86.6 %, and reach 99.3 % on the SIPaKMeD medical dataset, offloading 99.7 % of convolutional multiply‐accumulate operations to optics. By removing volumetric diffractive layers, this work enables low‐latency hybrid optoelectronic edge intelligent vision.

title: Simulation-Based LQR-Trees for Swing-Up Control of a Double Pendulum on a Cart: A MATLAB Implementation
abstract: Simülasyon Tabanlı LQR-Ağaçları ile Araba - Çift Sarkaç Sisteminin Salınım Kontrolü: Bir MATLAB Gerçeklemesi ÖzetçeBu çalışmada, araba üzerindeki çift sarkacın geniş bir başlangıç koşulu kümesinden yukarı denge konumuna taşınması için simülasyon tabanlı LQR-Ağaçları yaklaşımı benimsenmiş ve MATLAB ortamında yeniden üretilmiştir. Yeniden üretim sırasında referans çalışmanın yöntemi bir dizi revizyonla geliştirilmiştir. Referans yörüngeler Hermite–Simpson kollokasyonu ve fizibilite öncelikli üç aşamalı bir çözüm akışıyla üretilmiş, her yörünge zamana bağlı LQR ile kararlılaştırılmış, huni başlangıç kümeleri uyarlanır halka genişletmeli ızgara taramasıyla yaklaşıklanmış ve kapsama ölçütüne araba konum kısıtı dahil edilmiştir. Beş rastgele tohumla büyütülen 40 yörüngelik ağaçlar tasarım kümesinin ortalama %83.8'ini kapsamış (referans çalışma: %83), hibrit strateji 500 rastgele başlangıcın %95.2'sini kısıt ihlalsiz olarak üst denge konumuna oturtmuştur. Huniye girişleri iç hücrelerle sınırlayan kural, seyrek gözlenen ıraksama modunu tümüyle gidererek başarı oranını %98.6'ya yükseltmiştir. Simulation-Based LQR-Trees for Swing-Up Control of a Double Pendulum on a Cart: A MATLAB Implementation AbstractIn this study, the simulation-based LQR-Trees approach is adopted and reproduced in MATLAB to swing up a cart-mounted double pendulum from a wide set of initial conditions to the upright equilibrium. In the course of this reproduction, the method of the reference study is enhanced through several revisions. Reference trajectories are generated using Hermite–Simpson collocation and a feasibility-first three-stage solution framework, while each trajectory is stabilized by time-varying LQR. Funnel initial sets are approximated through adaptive ring-expansion grid sampling, and a cart-position constraint is incorporated into the coverage criterion. Trees grown with five random seeds and 40 trajectories each cover on average 83.8% of the design set (reference study: 83%), and the hybrid strategy stabilizes 95.2% of 500 random initial states at the upright equilibrium without constraint violations. A membership rule restricting funnel entry to interior cells eliminates a rarely observed divergence mode and raises the success rate to 98.6%.

title: Artificial Human: Genuine Need as a Precondition for Genuine AGI
abstract: We argue that a system with substantial processing capacity can be a genuine artificial general intelligence (AGI) — an independent agent rather than a computing system — only if its processing is coupled to a genuine need. We call a system that satisfies this condition an artificial human. Our claims are three. First, processing alone is not enough and need alone is not enough: genuine need must sit alongside processing (c = p·b; Rezaei, 2026a), and an AGI without genuine need is, on our view, a computing system and not an independent person. Second, the architecture must be two-loop, in the form of AIWBN (Rezaei, 2026b): the processing loop must not be able to access, suppress, or route around the need loop, and if the need is neutralized by any fixed method so that b = 0, the system’s will to continue must go out with it rather than persist on some residual objective. Third, the nature of genuine need is left open: our assumption is that it is derived from life, but we do not claim this, we do not reject other domains, and the one condition we do claim is that the need be real — not a label. The paper is narrower than AIWBN, which concerned need grounded in living tissue, and it neither rejects nor depends on AIWAN (Rezaei, 2026c), which concerned artificial need. We do not claim that genuine need would make an artificial system benevolent, and we do not address safety. No experiment is reported for the central claim, because it first requires an answer to what genuine need is and an inseparable bond between algorithm and need; we instead summarize selected AIWAN experiments that motivate the architectural requirements.

title: ViMoLa: Discrete Motion Tokens for Language-Guided Video Generation
abstract: Language-guided video generation often captures scene content while missing the requested motion. We present ViMoLa (Video Motion Language), which predicts a motion prior from language and injects it into a frozen image-to-video backbone. A spatial vector-quantized autoencoder compresses dense trajectories into 64 tokens from a 512-entry codebook; a 28M-parameter transformer predicts the tokens from text; and zero-gated cross-attention adapters condition every frozen Wan~2.2 DiT block through forward hooks. Trained on 462K videos from Something-Something~v2 and Kinetics-400, ViMoLa raises directional accuracy from 0.287 to 0.442 (chance 0.250), with similar measured generative quality. Across-prompt shuffled codes achieve 0.283, supporting the importance of prompt-matched token content. A low-rank adapter reaches 0.428 at 1.45% additional forward-pass FLOPs, and reusing the tokenizer and language model with newly trained CogVideoX adapters raises accuracy from 0.301 to 0.398. Control remains imperfect: oracle codes reach 0.531, compound-motion gains are smaller, and the adapter does not explicitly preserve token-to-patch assignments.

title: StopLoss: Teaching Agents to Predict Failure and Stop Early
abstract: Coding agents keep working on runs that will fail verification, and asking a frontier model to watch for this is expensive in its own right. We introduce StopLoss, a small external monitor that learns failure recognition from completed trajectories and their verifier outcomes. The name is inspired by the stop-loss order in finance: StopLoss ends a run early when the run is likely to fail, which saves resources. Final outcomes label earlier local windows, so a fine-tuned language model can score the most recent tool steps in a single forward pass, and a threshold calibrated on successful runs turns that score into an abort decision without changing the executor. Trained on GPT-family SWE-rebench trajectories and evaluated on SWE-bench Verified and a SWE-bench Pro subset with GPT and Claude executors, StopLoss is compared against six general-purpose judges reading identical windows. Outcome supervision lifts failure prediction from near chance to a useful signal at the first check, at one to two orders of magnitude lower cost per check than any tested judge. This translates into savings: relative to completing every task, StopLoss lowers cost per retained solve by 4.5\% on Verified while preserving 99\% of successful runs, and by up to 31\% on the costlier Pro subset, reaching 48\% with a Qwen3-8B backbone, and in all four settings its cost per retained solve is below that of every judge policy. Outcome-trained small monitors can make failure recognition cheap enough for early stopping to pay for itself.

title: Continuation under Incompleteness. Proven Reliability, Settling-In and Branchable Development of Autonomous Systems
abstract: This independently readable companion paper extends the conceptual synthesis and discussion paper “Robotics Capable of Development” by examining the temporal development of reliable competences, local settling-in, responsibility and the continuation of autonomous systems under incomplete knowledge. A robot operating for extended periods in an open human environment cannot know every future condition in advance or possess every required competence as a fully specified rule from the outset. The paper therefore asks how abilities are acquired, how their reliability is demonstrated in practice and how the conditions and limits of their validity can remain recognizable during operation. Central distinctions concern competence, proven reliability and authorization, as well as general training and local settling-in. Other topics include historically established reliability, trust, responsible action under uncertainty, the interests of affected third parties, and the possibility of revising established routines when the world changes. A further focus is the continuation of artificial development after interruptions. The paper discusses the preservation of Gewordenheit, selective memory, reconnection after disruptions, backups, changes of physical carrier and branchable artificial ontogeny, in which shared developmental states can give rise to different subsequent learning histories. The paper presents neither a finished technical architecture nor a systematic literature review, and it makes no claim of scientific priority. Its purpose is to connect conceptual distinctions, research questions, possible experiments and counter-hypotheses that may help investigate the conditions of responsible, reliable and developmentally open autonomy.

title: BiDex-100: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation Across 100+ Simulation Tasks
abstract: Bimanual manipulation with dexterous hands has attracted growing attention in research on robotic action models. However, few studies have developed benchmarks specifically tailored for dexterous manipulation, leaving the dexterous manipulation capabilities of existing models insufficiently characterized. In this paper, we present BiDex-100, a simulation benchmark for bimanual dexterous manipulation that combines broad task coverage, multi-dimensional evaluation, and high-DoF hand embodiments. Concretely, the benchmark comprises 106 tasks organized along five capability axes: generalization, instruction following, limited demonstrations, long horizon, and memory. Each task is paired with an out-of-domain variant featuring controlled visual and spatial changes, allowing systematic assessment of robustness. In addition, the benchmark supports two embodiments and provides 8,080 success-validated teleoperated demonstrations, totaling 6.25 million frames. We evaluate seven recent Vision-Language-Action models under a unified protocol, establishing baselines for capability-specific performance, robustness, and data efficiency. The website is available at https://BiDex-100.github.io/BiDex-100/.

title: THE REFERENCE-RELATIVE REALIZATION PRINCIPLE (RRRP): A General Reference-Relative Systems Principle with a Paradoxical Regime
abstract: The Reference-Relative Realization Principle (RRRP) proposes a general systems framework inin which the realization of a state, function, signal, representation, process, or output is defined relativeto an explicit reference structure rather than as an absolute property of the system alone. The theoryoriginates from the primary case study The Paradox of Contextualism, in which a subjectively specifiedintention may be evaluated by a generalized system through a reference structure that does not coincidewith the source-intended structure. The resulting apparent contradiction is not treated as a universalimpossibility theorem: exact realization can occur when the relevant equivalence relation is preserved,whereas non-equivalence between source and target reference structures makes exact preservation non-guaranteed. The framework therefore separates default mechanism, generalized principle, and paradoxicalor divergent regimes. A unified architecture represents source formation, encoding, labeling, signaling,projection, processing, medium transformation, target reconstruction, reference-relative evaluation,residual formation, iterative adaptation, and network-level interaction. The model is independent ofany particular criterion or medium: security, accuracy, utility, stability, semantic fidelity, energy, timing,language, code, physical channels, mathematical notation, computational systems, quantum systems,biological systems, and other admissible cases enter as parameterized instances. A finite operationalregime is complemented by an asymptotic regime for iterative realization. Thirty extension case studiesare organized across three analytical layers: Philosophical-Epistemological, Systemic-Mechanistic, andFormal-Mathematical Operational. The manuscript explicitly distinguishes mathematical definitionfrom empirical claim, identifies boundary conditions and counterexamples, and provides a falsifiabilityand anti-pseudomathematics protocol. The result is a general relational principle rather than a claim ofa universal physical law.

title: System X: An LLM Decision Model That Replies from Its Own KV Cache
abstract: Decision models return probabilities over supplied options, but a deployed agent may also need to reply in words. The present study introduces System X, a large language model (LLM) decision model that adds a text-reply option to the LLM-as-Jev readout. When this option wins, or confidence is low, the same model continues from the decision's key-value (KV) cache, avoiding a repeated prompt prefill. Qwen3-0.6B has been fine-tuned with LoRA on Reason-9k and Bitext reply rows. JevBench accuracy shows no statistically significant change (55.4% to 54.5%, p=0.87), while expected calibration error falls from 0.292 to 0.169. Held-out Bitext routing accuracy reaches 98.3%. Cache reuse saves 15-37% of latency on an Apple M4 Pro, with token-identical replies in the FP32 demonstration cases. Scoring options on copies of the prompt cache matches full-sequence scoring to within 1.4e-6 in probability. Adding dialogue, industry and complaint data (System X+) improves support-task results but lowers IFEval accuracy from 55.5% to 45.0%. System X v4 uses Qwen3-1.7B, rebalanced data and teacher-rewritten reply targets. Against its base LLM, JevBench accuracy rises from 55.0% to 61.0% (p=0.04), with no statistically significant IFEval change (p=0.71). A matched latency test on unadapted Qwen3-1.7B saves 17-39%. One LLM judge prefers v4 replies to an unadapted 1.7B second call (31 to 11 pairs, p=0.003); the other's preference is not significant. These reply comparisons also differ in prompts and generation limits. State conflicts and unsupported reply details remain failure modes. Further studies with several seeds, human raters and real support data are recommended.

title: BLLM: The Entropy Cost of Sound Self-Improvement and a Typed Crossing Network Tested on Five Open Problems: paper, Lean 4 formalization and verification code
abstract: A BLLM is a language model that keeps a modification of itself only after a randomized check of soundness epsilon accepts it. The paper proves that certifying modifications of total cost A with at most theta expected false acceptances costs (A/log(1/epsilon))(H(p) + log(1/theta)) up to an additive A, where H(p) is the entropy of the cost profile; that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when the sum of a_n log(1/a_n) converges; and that a proposer needs at least exp(H_{1/2}(pi)) proposals, a bound that language models miss by factors of 1.5 to 4.3. It also describes and measures a typed crossing network with shared memory, run on five open problems (the Yang-Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture and Erdos problem 1183): the network reaches what its libraries can reach with half the checks, Hebbian boosters add nothing, and none of the five problems is solved. The lattice mass gap for four-dimensional SU(2) on beta_W < 1/3 is proved in the paper and has not been refereed. preprintBeyondTheLLM/ holds the paper as a PDF; BLLM/paper/ holds the REVTeX source with its figures; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip and the arXiv tarball. BLLM/lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib project with fifty-nine theorems, each depending only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. BLLM/checks/ contains independent checks in Python, C and C++ (55,271 checks); BLLM/checks/run_all.sh runs them and builds the Lean project. The benchmark, the crossing network and the logs of every run are in the package eBLLM, version 2.0.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23455686.

title: RARE: Reinforcement Learning with Adaptive Rubric Evolution for Open-Ended Generation
abstract: Verifiable rewards have advanced reinforcement learning in mathematics and code. However, many valuable open-ended tasks share three properties: no automatic verifier of overall quality, multiple requirements to satisfy jointly, and multiple valid responses to each query. Training therefore needs feedback on requirement satisfaction across different valid responses. Rubric-based reinforcement learning provides this feedback by aggregating scores from explicit criteria. As learning progresses unevenly, some criteria become fully satisfied and lose discrimination while others remain informative. Dynamic methods revise shared rubrics or select evolving criteria to restore discrimination, but may also change useful criteria. To address this, we propose Reinforcement Learning with Adaptive Rubric Evolution (RARE). The core idea is to use current policy feedback to guide both which criteria change and what their replacements assess. Sample-level updates replace criteria fully satisfied across current outputs with checks of remaining quality differences, retaining all other criteria and scores. Within this rule, we compare rewarding desirable qualities with penalizing observed flaws. Video script generation exemplifies these properties and supports content production. Its demands for coherent, executable narratives under constraints make it a challenging testbed. Targeting flaws performs best across three video types with a mean gain of 3.82 points over matched static rubrics. Model and human preferences support these gains. Improvements also extend to writing and general generation benchmarks.

title: Mixture-of-Memories: Low-Overhead Language Modeling with Modular Knowledge Injection
abstract: Large language models store substantial factual knowledge in their parameters, yet this knowledge is difficult to control, update, and reliably elicit at inference time. Existing memory-augmented approaches typically rely on a single auxiliary mechanism, such as retrieval, parameter updates, or neural memory, and therefore apply the same form of correction to tokens with very different knowledge demands. We propose Mixture-of-Memories (MoM), a memory-augmented language modeling framework that separates routed neural memory from writable factual memory. MoM combines a frozen base LM with two neural memory experts: a latent memory that provides low-latency hidden-state corrections and a lexical memory that provides a token-space knowledge pathway. A lightweight Budget Router sets per-token mixture weights from uncertainty and disagreement features, replacing the fixed interpolation of prior memory modules. For post-hoc updates, an external explicit memory stays outside the router, because a router trained before facts are written learns to down-weight it; new facts are appended without retraining any component and used only when an answer-level gate accepts the retrieved fact. Experiments across language modeling, factual QA, update analysis, and efficiency show that MoM improves both predictive accuracy and updateability while retaining low inference overhead.

title: MT Forcing: Towards Stable and Consistent Multi-Turn Image Editing with Autoregressive Diffusion
abstract: Multi-turn image editing aims to modify an image according to a sequence of instructions, enabling more effective interactive visual content creation for users. However, existing methods often exhibit noticeable drift after only a few editing turns, manifesting in two aspects: 1) unstable visual quality, with accumulating artifacts and degraded details; and 2) inconsistent image content, with unintended changes to preserved regions and prior edits. To address these challenges, we propose MT Forcing, a novel training paradigm for multi-turn image editing with unified multimodal models (UMMs) based on autoregressive diffusion. Specifically, we propose Single-Turn Distribution Matching Distillation (Single-Turn DMD), which supervises student self-rollouts with a teacher that applies cumulative edits to the source image in a single turn, providing visual-quality guidance without recursive error accumulation. Additionally, we introduce Teacher-Forcing Guidance, which supervises history-dependent transitions on reference trajectories during warmup and as a regularizer during distillation, encouraging cross-turn content consistency beyond what per-turn distribution matching alone can ensure. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly improves the multi-turn image editing capabilities of UMMs, yielding more stable visual quality and stronger cross-turn consistency.

title: Whistle and Wrong Lyrics: Synthetic Queries Are Not Enough for Real-World Query-by-Melody
abstract: People look up a song by humming it, but also by whistling it or singing it with the wrong words. Published query-by-humming systems and benchmarks focus on hums and sung queries, and no public dataset pairs whistles or wrong-lyrics singing with song recordings. We study both query types with a melody-only retrieval system: a key-normalized pitch track embedded by a 5.2M-parameter contour encoder, with a spectral-peak tracker for whistles. First, a physics-grounded generator renders synthetic whistles and nonsense-syllable singing from the vocal melodies of 11,083 songs. Training on them raises top-1 retrieval of held-out synthetic queries against an 11,050-song gallery from 0.180 to 0.251 for whistles and from 0.193 to 0.264 for wrong-lyrics singing, but the gain does not transfer: on the MLEnd test performers the best synthetic-only model gets 210 of 339 real whistles right at top-1, against 214 for the baseline. Second, a closed-set fine-tune on real MLEnd whistles with performer-disjoint splits raises whistle-to-hum top-1 from 0.631 (95% CI 0.581-0.681) to 0.673 (0.622-0.723), on known songs only. Third, two further generations of synthetic queries also fail to transfer: melody-conditioned whistles and la-la singing from a commercial neural music model leave real-whistle top-1 at 0.631, and an open-source pipeline (YingMusic-Singer-Plus singing with partly wrong, mumbled or nonsense lyrics, a DDSP whistle synthesizer, and a melody-error model fitted on real performers) gives at best 0.619 (paired difference -0.012, 95% CI -0.038 to +0.015). Across physics-based, commercial neural and open-source neural synthetic data, nothing transferred to real whistles, which points to collecting real queries as the missing step. Code is public; models and data will be released.

title: E8 Triadic Entanglement Protocol for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Networks — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 240 root vectors of the E8 lattice partition into 72 triadic triplets, each resonating at the 132 Hz base frequency and its phi‑harmonics, providing a natural encoding for logical qubits. By exploiting the high symmetry of E8, these triplets generate entangled states that are intrinsically resistant to phase errors, enabling fault‑tolerant quantum communication. The phi‑coupling between adjacent triplets ensures error cancellation across the network, while the 132 Hz global clock synchronizes distributed nodes. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: MCSplat: Multi-View Photometric and Geometric Consistent Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for Driving Scenes
abstract: Driving-scene reconstruction via feed-forward Gaussian splatting from sparse multi-view images remains challenging due to two factors. First, cross-camera photometric inconsistency, caused by variations in exposure, ISP, and illumination, can be incorrectly absorbed into Gaussian geometry. Second, unreliable local geometric supervision arises from normal-based constraints near depth discontinuities. To address these issues, we present MCSplat, a multi-view consistent feed-forward Gaussian splatting framework for driving scenes. MCSplat constructs a canonical appearance space from depth-guided multi-camera correspondences to decouple geometry learning from camera-specific appearance. A multi-scale Bilateral Grid Transformer restores raw camera appearance from canonical renderings, enabling photometric supervision without contaminating Gaussian geometry. To improve local geometric reliability, we estimate Fisher-information-based uncertainty from photometric sensitivity and use it to adaptively weight surface-oriented self-supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and generalization across driving datasets. Geometry-oriented evaluations further reveal enhanced cross-view depth consistency and local surface-normal agreement, while qualitative results show fewer geometric artifacts and more coherent structures across overlapping views.

title: The Economic Value of AI-Driven Customer Experience in Digital Business Models
abstract: AI was increasingly revolutionizing digital business models by delivering superior customer experience and creating identifiable financial value. This study sought to understand the economic consequences of AI-enabled customer experience on digital media platforms in terms of consumer mindset, business functionality, and competitive edge. The purpose was to investigate how AI enhances customer interaction, what it contributes economically in terms of cost-cutting and increased profits, as well as identification of challenges, threats, and future trends. A quantitative research design was adopted, and a structured questionnaire was distributed to 250 users of digital business service. The results demonstrated that AI was found to facilitate increased customer satisfaction, transaction time saving and personalization and thus led to greater inclination of spending and loyalty. A ranking analysis showed that the most valued outcomes were cost savings and customer satisfaction, and the former was found to be the most preferred. Results indicated that the firms that integrated AI had received a more positive brand reputation and competitive advantage than those without. The report found that AI-based customer experience had generated significant economic value, but also encountered challenges in trust, data security and implementation cost continued to be challenging.

title: World Model Interpretability: From Decoding Representations to Understanding Latent Worlds
abstract: Emerging Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) are moving beyond representation learning towards latent world models that support prediction, planning, and control. Yet their latent worlds naturally lack a human-interpretable interface. In this Perspective, we argue that as JEPA latents become internal states for prediction and action, interpretability must move beyond what they encode to how latent variables interact, evolve, and causally drive prediction. To this end, we envision a four-stage research agenda, involving Ground, Structure, Verify, and Act, to guide this shift toward actionable latent-world understanding. Within our framework, existing JEPA interpretability efforts provide early evidence for Ground, while systematic analysis of latent structure, causal verification, and intervention remains largely unexplored. Overall, this Perspective aims to call for a broader latent-world interpretability agenda that shifts attention from decoding representations toward understanding, validating, and acting on latent worlds.

title: Human-in-Command (HIC) Governance for Generative AI Copyright and Physical-Layer Defense — Mathematical Formalization of $10B-Scale TCO Optimization, Decoupled Cluster/Unlearning Data Shapley, CLAP Multi-Stem Audio Attribution, Sub-1.5-ms HIC-CBF-QP Subsea Rerouting under UNCLOS, QPUF Silicon Root of Trust, and NIST FIPS 203 (ML-KEM-768) Edge TEE Provenance

title: SPARC: Spoken Profile Authorship Recognition Corpus
abstract: Speech anonymization has focused on the acoustic signal, leaving open how much speaker information the transcribed words themselves retain. In this work, we study pairwise speaker and demographic-attribute verification from transcribed speech. We introduce SPARC (Spoken Profile Authorship Recognition Corpus), a benchmark built from two podcast corpora comprising over 12,500 speakers, 1.5M quality-filtered utterances, and speaker-level inferred or source-provided labels for sex, age, and accent, and evaluate five attribution models and three LLMs on identity- and attribute-verification trials with episode- and metadata-based topic proxies. LLM adversaries distinguish same-speaker pairs from text alone. Attribute-label agreement is harder to verify, but LLMs perform sex- and accent-label verification above chance. Finally, releasing only short probe texts (50 words) degrades the strongest adversaries the most, offering a partial reduction in observed linkage.

title: Persistent Representational Misalignment Induces Vision-Language Model Failures
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) fail at some tasks that are simple for humans---but why? We hypothesize that many such failures stem from VLMs' difficulties translating between vision and language representations, a misalignment the Platonic Representation Hypothesis predicts should disappear with scale. This paper is composed of two parts: in the first, we show that existing vision and language representations are linearly unalignable. This misalignment is an inherent property of the data and hence expected to persist regardless of either scale or the alignment's complexity. In the second, we demonstrate how this misalignment both leads to a predictably induced generalization failure and correlates with existing failure modes, where more representationally aligned VLM backbones accordingly exhibit fewer failures. Overall, these results imply representations will not become aligned simply given sufficient scale, providing evidence against a strong version of the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.

title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality-Emotional Attachment-Loyalty Pathway in 2025-2026
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although the retailer-specific investment figures cited in an earlier draft have not been independently substantiated. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). We discuss a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.
